name: Kheema Par Eeda
subtitle: spiced mutton mince with eggs baked into the surface, soft yolks over dry kheema
prepNotes: Use a wide pan with a lid. You need enough surface area to sit four eggs apart from each other.
Bring the eggs to room temperature so the whites set evenly on the hot kheema.
The kheema must be dry before the eggs go on. Wet mince makes the whites run together into a puddle.

steps.text: Heat the ghee in a wide kadhai and fry the onion until golden brown, 12 minutes.
Add ginger, garlic and green chilli and fry 2 minutes.
Add turmeric, chilli powder, coriander and cumin powder, and fry 30 seconds.
Add the mince and break it up with the back of a spoon, frying 8 minutes until it loses all pinkness and starts to catch.
steps.tip: Break the lumps early. Once the mince sets in clumps you will not get it smooth again.

steps.text: Add the tomato and salt and cook 6 minutes until the tomato disappears into the mince.
Add the water, cover, and simmer 12 minutes, then uncover and cook off every trace of liquid, about 5 minutes.
steps.tip: Dry means dry. Tilt the pan and no gravy should run.

steps.text: Stir through the garam masala, coriander leaves and mint, then level the surface and press four shallow wells with the back of a spoon.
Crack an egg into each well, season with salt and the coarse black pepper.
Cover and cook on the lowest heat 8-10 minutes, until the whites are opaque and the yolks still wobble.
steps.tip: Check at 8 minutes. A minute too long and you lose the runny yolk that makes the dish.

steps.text: Bring the pan to the table and serve with pav or rotli.

storage: Best eaten straight away for the soft yolks. Leftover kheema alone keeps 2 days refrigerated; reheat and crack fresh eggs onto it.
